title: A portrait
takeaway: Missing someone can make you as still as a picture.
scene: A single couplet. The poet looks at a picture of the person he loves.

original: آج دیکھ کے یار تصویر تیری بن گیا ہاں وانگ تصویر میں وی
روسے تیرے نے جگ ہنیر کیتا دل لئی پھرنا اک دلگیر میں وی
transliteration: Ajj dekh ke yaar tasveer teri, ban gaya haan vaang tasveer main vi
Rosse tere ne jag haner keeta, dil layi phirna ik dilgeer main vi
translation: Today, looking at your picture, my friend, I've become still as a picture myself.
Your sulking has darkened the world; I too go around carrying a heavy heart.
couplets.story: Looking at the Beloved's photo today, he froze, as still as a picture himself. Because the Beloved is upset with him, the whole world feels dark, and he walks around with a heavy heart.

deeper: A tiny love poem. Read the Sufi way, the Beloved's 'sulking' is the feeling that God has gone quiet. Sufis call it qabz, a tightening of the heart. The world goes dark, and the seeker can only stand still and wait.
why: A single couplet with a striking image: looking at a picture until you become one.
prompt: Is there a photo that makes you stop and stare? What does it remind you of?
